title: Physics of the flying fish: glide data and Thompson's flight envelope
headline: The flying fish is inside Thompson's envelope: from its own measured wing loading and lift coefficient (Park and Choi 2010) its minimum lift-supported speed is 9.85 m/s, and quoted field glide speeds are 10 to 20 m/s. The scaling law itself (speed grows as the square root of wing loading) is inconclusive on the data we could reach: 2 glider taxa and 6 powered-flier taxa with both numbers, the latter spanning 0.93 decades of wing loading against the pre-registered minimum of 1. Whether fin muscles could power level flight cannot be told: no source gives the muscle numbers. The #50 glide table has 27 rows from 7 fetched sources; no accessible source gives mass, fin area and a measured airspeed for the same fish, which is the finding. Birds excluded (Aves holdout). Pre-registered before any value was read; 97 logged searches and fetches; OpenAlex was rate-limited so Europe PMC and Crossref carried the search.
